page_title: Berthly — a native macOS GUI for Apple's container

sources.entry: Berthly - Native GUI for Apple's container tool, with menu bar monitoring and drag-and-drop image builds. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/henrywang/Berthly) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Berthly
summary.one_liner: Berthly is a native macOS GUI app for Apple's container tool that lets you build images, run containers and machines, manage networks and volumes, and view logs without using the command line.
use_cases: manage Linux containers on a Mac without the command line
build images from a Dockerfile via drag and drop
monitor container CPU, memory and network usage
check registries for updated images and recreate containers
manage Apple container machines and kernels
summary.what_it_does: Berthly is a macOS app that provides a graphical interface over Apple's container tool and its daemon. It can pull, build, inspect and list images, create and run containers, and manage machines (VMs), networks and volumes. Containers get live CPU, memory and network charts, and logs stream as they happen, with an integrated terminal built on SwiftTerm. Dragging a Dockerfile or Containerfile onto the window opens a pre-filled Build sheet, and build context and flags are remembered for rebuilds. It checks registries in the background and flags images whose registry digest has changed.
notable: Drag-and-drop Dockerfile/Containerfile builds from Finder, with remembered build flags for one-click rebuilds
Menu bar monitoring and notifications when pinned containers change state
Keyboard-first design with a ⌘K command palette
Open source under Apache-2.0; credentials stored in macOS Keychain and no telemetry
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or later
Requires Apple's container daemon; Berthly installs its toolchain if none is present
Not sandboxed, by necessity, according to the page
